jobs.title: Manager of Enterprise Open Source Sales Team
jobs.excerpt: Open source software is the new default in the enterprise, and Canonical is the new challenger to major enterprise software vendors.
jobs.description:
Open source software is the new default in the enterprise, and Canonical is the new challenger to major enterprise software vendors.

We are profitable and growing our global enterprise sales organisation. We are hiring regional sales team managers in Europe, Middle East, India, Asia, ANZ, Africa, Latin America, Central America and North America, each of whom will lead a team of five to ten enterprise sales representatives.

We deliver better open source from the data center to cloud and edge. Our Linux distribution Ubuntu is now the leading platform for public cloud compute, and the favorite platform for software engineers, data scientists and AI developers. Our mission is to accelerate the adoption and quality of open source globally, and our goal is to ship the most software on the planet by cores. A tidal wave of open source innovation is the next phase of the entire enterprise software industry, and we aim to be the most compelling way to ride that wave.

Our customers include Global 500 enterprises and startups. We are expanding our product range from the base operating system - Ubuntu - to full enterprise solutions in infrastructure and applications. We can deliver software defined storage, private cloud solutions, container runtime environments, as well as databases, message queues, identity, observability, analytics, machine learning and web publishing capabilities. Customers love the idea that they can get security compliance and support for everything open source from a single company. Our goal is to have more solutions on tap than any other vendor, and we have built unique capabilities to make that possible across every cloud, every class of compute and every category of application.

Canonical provides licensed enterprise software products, commercial support, managed services, consulting and training services to customers who are deploying Ubuntu or open source applications on the cloud, in their data center, or to the connected device and IoT ecosystem. We are just over 1,000 colleagues in 70+ countries and over $250m in revenue, profitable, on a steady but relentless growth trajectory. We are almost entirely distributed, with leadership spread across many countries. We believe that talent is equally distributed across the globe, and we are excited to hire, develop, promote and ultimately trust a diverse group of exceptional leads to build the best, not biggest, enterprise software company.

We hire carefully and deliberately; our selection process is long and requires substantial work from applicants. It will take successful applicants three to six months to secure an offer. This is not a place to apply if you are in a rush to find a position, it is a worthwhile place to apply if you are ambitious and long-term in your thinking about your career and the dynamics which move the world forward. If you see clearly the rise of open source, and you understand the drivers of enterprise procurement and technical decision making, then you will understand why Canonical has such a tremendous long term advantage. You will also understand, given the ferocity of competition and the challenges of competing in a market of giants, that we have to set a very high bar for hiring and performance. In order to be a world leading company we select for exceptional ability as well as character, and then provide an environment which promotes teamwork and celebrates diligence, collaboration and effectiveness. All of those are easy to say but hard to do - at Canonical we are willing to be uncomfortable in pursuit of that excellence.

In building our sales team, we look for five things:

  • Empathy for the customer - a real understanding of customer needs, industry-specific challenges, and a desire to help customers solve their business problems
  • High intellect - the ability to learn quickly, understand very complex subjects, and communicate clearly to build trust and confidence
  • Passion for technology - a fascination with the state of the art from brilliant people solving hard problems, and fierce competition for large prizes
  • Teamwork - a willingness to help others, to collaborate well with people from different disciplines, and to balance personal and team ambitions
  • Energy - the drive to motivate oneself and others to achieve the best result for the team and our customers

Ubuntu is already very widely adopted which gives us a credible basis for conversations in the market. Nevertheless, it requires real work for sales professionals to build on that adoption to create trusted and profitable commercial relationships with the enterprises in their territory. Our product managers and marketing teams run campaigns to generate awareness, engagement and leads, but you will need to go beyond managing inbound interest to develop the potential of your territory. You will need judgement as to which industries and companies are ready to go deeper with open source and Canonical, and energy to develop relationships in advance of proven interest. We expect professional practice, territory and account planning, as well as clear, complete and continuous reporting on pipeline status and activity, using standard professional tools.

The successful candidate will carry an annual team bookings quota within their territory. They should be able to travel regionally for client engagements or, industry conferences, and internationally for company events twice a year. They will be expected to demonstrate professionalism and effectiveness in managing their team. They will need to coach, mentor and lead by example. Their sales representatives are expected to prospect accounts for new business, maintain and develop existing relationships, and work with colleagues and partners on account strategy. They must be comfortable selling enterprise software, open source, cloud, virtualization, container technologies and technical software solutions to senior levels of the enterprise.

Location: We are expanding our sales organisation globally and have open sales team manager roles in every region.

What your day will look like

  • Build and execute a territory plan to prioritize outreach and prospecting
  • Allocate portions of territory and accounts to sales representatives on your team
  • Identify and prioritise new logo accounts in your territory for account-based marketing and prospecting
  • Ensure that sales representatives have high quality account plans for existing accounts and priority prospects
  • Monitor new pipeline development by your team, through outreach, prospecting, local marketing, and industry events
  • Support contract closure to meet and exceed quarterly and annual bookings targets
  • Be mindful and proactive in achieving tactical and strategic objectives
  • Work with customer success to identify growth opportunities
  • Ensure your team maintain accurate pipeline data and forecasts within Salesforce
  • Represent the company, its solutions and software

What we are looking for in you

  • Bachelor's level degree, preferably in engineering or computer science
  • Leadership and management skill
  • Experience of open source technology and solutions
  • Detail oriented with effective planning, organisation and reporting skill
  • Experience in enterprise software or technology sales planning and execution
  • Track record of achievement in sales targets and new account wins
  • Self-discipline and motivation to be successful in a distributed team
  • Professional written and spoken English, as well as any language that may be appropriate for your target market
  • Ability to travel for customer engagements, industry events and company events

Additional skills of interest

  • Specific vertical experience, in particular finance, telco, health, energy, public sector, tech
  • Experience speaking at conferences or industry events

What we offer you

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance when shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven commission structure. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team meetings in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Canonical has been a fully distributed company since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

Every therapist on the remote caseload starts with six in-person brace fittings on patients from your own current caseload, so you know the devices you will be coaching patients on. jobs.description:
About us

Founded in 1996, Argos Multilingual is a global provider of technology-enabled language, AI and data solutions. We combine human expertise, technology and AI to help organisations communicate, operate and grow across markets.

We work with some of the world’s most recognised companies, from global technology leaders and e-commerce innovators to major organisations in life sciences and manufacturing. Our clients operate at significant scale, giving our people the opportunity to work on complex, high-impact projects.

With 400+ people across 42 countries, cultures and time zones, we are a truly international organisation. We are continuing to expand our capabilities in AI and data alongside our established language and localisation expertise, building on a strong foundation while embracing the opportunities created by new technology.

About the role

Few L&D roles give you the chance to reimagine an entire training library with AI and modern tools. This one does. As our L&D Specialist, you’ll turn fresh ideas into courses people actually want to take, creating learning faster and, above all, building real capability across our workforce. You’ll be one of a two-person L&D team reporting directly to our SVP HR (Head of HR), with real independence and the backing to try new approaches. What you build will shape how hundreds of colleagues learn and grow.

What you'll do

  • Rebuild and modernise our training library with innovative content, recommending what to update, redesign or retire, and drive continuous improvement by tracking industry trends and internal metrics and testing new formats and tools.
  • Plan, organise and deliver training of all kinds, including technical training: build e-learning courses, live sessions, workshops, manuals and knowledge resources in line with the annual L&D plan, and keep them up to date as our tools and processes change.
  • Manage the day-to-day administration of our LMS (currently TalentLMS) and maintain the compliance training matrix, tracking completion and keeping evidence ready for internal and external ISO audits.
  • Coordinate and deliver onboarding training for new hires, and keep improving how we bring people up to speed.
  • Measure impact using models such as Kirkpatrick, run training needs and satisfaction surveys, track L&D KPIs and report clearly to the SVP HR and stakeholders.
  • Manage several training projects at once, building strong working relationships with product owners, managers and subject-matter experts, and coaching internal experts to deliver training well (train-the-trainer).
  • Work closely with the HR team on wider initiatives, such as system implementations and documentation, and take on other related duties as assigned to support HR, L&D and organisational goals.

Skills & Experience

  • 5+ years of hands-on L&D experience in a global organisation, in any industry (technology preferred).
  • Strong experience administering an LMS, LXP or similar platform.
  • Proven experience building e-learning and delivering live training, grounded in learning design principles.
  • Hands-on experience using AI and modern authoring tools to build learning content (for example Articulate 360, Synthesia, Vyond or Camtasia).
  • Comfortable turning learning data into clear reports and insights.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Nice to have: TalentLMS, ISO compliance training, train-the-trainer programmes or evaluation models such as Kirkpatrick.
  • No localisation experience needed.

Who You Are

  • Dynamic and solutions-driven: you spot what isn’t working, fix it and get things moving.
  • A strong critical thinker who questions how things are done today, learns fast and takes initiative.
  • An owner who takes accountability for your work from start to finish.
  • Great at prioritising: you focus on what matters most and stay organised and detail-minded when plans change.
  • A clear, confident communicator who can influence managers and stakeholders at all levels.
  • Genuinely curious about how AI and new tools can make learning more effective and personalised.
  • Passionate about helping people reach their full potential.

Location

Argos is a remote-first, globally distributed organisation, with offices in seven countries, and we currently hire in 42 countries globally. This is a remote-based role, and you must have the legal right to work in your country. We do not provide sponsorship.

Why Join Us

You’ll be joining Argos at an important point in our growth and transformation. We have almost 30 years of experience and an established global client base, but we’re not interested in simply maintaining what we’ve built.

Our industry is changing rapidly. AI, data and technology are reshaping language and localisation, and we’re embracing that change by investing in new capabilities, exploring new ways of working and continuing to evolve our offering.

As part of a global, remote-first organisation, you’ll work with colleagues across countries, cultures and time zones, with the opportunity to learn from different perspectives and contribute to work with an international reach.

We offer the scale and stability of an established global business, combined with the opportunity to influence how we operate and where we go next. If you want to use your experience, challenge thinking and make a visible contribution rather than simply maintain the status quo, Argos offers the opportunity to do exactly that.

jobs.title: Medical Director, Clinical Communications
jobs.excerpt: About Lantern Lantern is the specialty care platform connecting people with the best care when they need it most.
jobs.description:
About Lantern

Lantern is the specialty care platform connecting people with the best care when they need it most. By curating a Network of Excellence comprised of the nation's top specialists for surgery, cancer care, infusions and more, Lantern delivers excellent care with significant cost savings to employers and their workforces. Lantern also pairs members with a dedicated care team, including Care Advocates and nurses, for the entirety of their care journey, helping them get back to good health, back to their families and back to work. With convenient access to specialists nationwide, Lantern means quality care is within driving distance for most. Lantern is trusted by the nation's largest employers to deliver care to more than 6 million members across the country. Learn more about us at lanterncare.com.

Medical Director, Clinical Communications

Lantern is looking for a Medical Director, Clinical Communications to join our Clinical team as the external voice of specialist qualification. Lantern operates a specialty care network built on a simple promise to clients and members: every specialist in our Network of Excellence has been evaluated, by procedure, against evidence-based clinical standards. The Clinical team sets those standards, runs the Qualification Committee, and is investing in the tooling and process that make qualification faster and more consistent for practices.

As that investment matures, the part of the process that will always require a human is the conversation with practices: explaining what we evaluate and why before a group applies, delivering approvals and procedure-level decisions clearly and respectfully, and giving groups that receive an adverse finding a credible explanation and a fair path to respond.

In this role you will own how qualification is explained, how decisions are delivered, and how practices experience the process. You will also bring the Clinical perspective into provider conversations and select client meetings and collaborate with the Provider Network team to educate and set our partner practices up for success. This is a Director-level individual contributor role, accountable for the entire qualification engagement function, with the potential to lead qualification operations staff as the function scales. This role suits two kinds of candidate: a seasoned credentialing, medical staff, or provider network leader, or a physician or surgeon ready to move from direct patient care into a high-impact role shaping network quality. What the role requires is credibility with surgeons and the judgment to deliver difficult clinical decisions well.

Location: Remote

Responsibilities:

Qualification decision communications:

  • Deliver every qualification, requalification, and standing-change decision to practices and specialists, including full approvals, procedure-level approvals, holds pending information, denials, and removals from the network.
  • Translate Qualification Committee reasoning into clear, accurate, clinically literate written and verbal communication that a practice administrator and a surgeon can both act on.
  • Own the adverse-finding workflow: request documentation or clarification from practices, track responses, bring complete information back to the Committee, and close the loop within defined service levels.
  • Handle pushback with composure and consistency, explaining the rationale and the published guideline review process, and escalate to the Associate CMO only when a case warrants clinical judgment beyond the guidelines.
  • Maintain the correspondence record so that any decision and its communication history can be reconstructed and audited.

Practice and specialist education:

  • Build and maintain the practice-facing explanation of qualification at Lantern: the seven quality domains we evaluate, the data sources we use, what the thresholds mean, and what a practice should expect at each stage.
  • Lead qualification overview conversations with prospective and newly contracted practices so that groups understand requirements before they invest effort and unqualified candidates are identified before contracting rather than after.
  • Set the qualification standard for Provider Success Managers, d so that they can answer first-line questions accurately and own the practice relationship without routing routine questions to Clinical.
  • Communicate guideline changes to affected practices and specialists, including re-evaluation pathways when standards evolve.

Qualification process operations:

  • Own the workflow from Committee decision to delivered communication, including letter generation from Prism, tracking, and turnaround reporting against the five-business day target from submission to decision.
  • Coordinate the Qualification Committee agenda and decision record in partnership with the Clinical Quality Manager and ensure the handoff to Network for placeability is clean and timely.
  • Capture and triage practice feedback.
  • Define and report the metrics that show whether the process is working.

Clinical representation on provider and client conversations:

  • Serve as the Clinical representative on provider calls that require clinical context, including qualification questions, clinical escalation feedback to practices, and specialist-facing quality discussions, with defined criteria for when a physician leader should join.
  • Represent the Clinical team on select commercial pitches and client conversations.

Function leadership:

  • Set the strategy, operating model, and service levels for qualification engagement, build the staffing case as volume grows, and represent the function in leadership forums alongside the Clinical team
  • Expected mix once ramped: roughly 70 to 80 percent qualification and practice-facing work, 20 to 30 percent provider and client representation. Commercial representation begins after the first 90 days.

Requirements:

  • You are a physician or surgeon (MD or DO), looking to apply your clinical judgment beyond direct patient care.
  • Credibility with surgeons. You command the respect of surgeons and practice leaders and can deliver difficult, clinically grounded decisions in a way that lands and keeps the relationship intact. We expect this to come from one of two backgrounds:
  • Exceptional communication. You write clearly and precisely, you explain complex criteria without jargon or condescension, and you can hold a hard conversation with a surgeon or practice executive and leave the relationship intact.
  • High emotional intelligence and judgment. You understand what a qualification decision means to a surgeon's identity, income, and reputation. You can be empathetic and firm at the same time, and you know when to listen, when to explain, and when to escalate.
  • Clinical literacy. Working knowledge of surgical specialties and procedures, how surgical practices operate, how surgeons are trained and credentialed, and how practice administrators, schedulers, and billing teams interact with payers and networks.
  • Independent problem solving and project management. You run multi-step processes with many stakeholders, track details without being asked, and improve the process rather than only operating it.
  • Comfort with data and tools. You can read a data-driven profile, understand what a volume threshold or an outcome metric means, spot an error before it reaches a practice, and work fluently in Microsoft 365 and modern software tools, including AI-assisted drafting with appropriate review.
  • Integrity under pressure. You hold the standard when a practice, a colleague, or a commercial deadline pushes for an exception, and you route that pressure into the proper review process.
  • Leadership and influence. You have set strategy for a function or program, influenced senior leaders and physicians without formal authority, and are ready to build and lead a team, or to grow into that as the function scales.

Strong Candidates will:

  • Have a clinical background: experience beyond direct patient care, such as medical directorship, utilization or peer review, committee or quality work, or clinical research.
  • Have built enablement or training materials for field or account teams.
  • Have presented to employer benefits leaders, consultants, or health plan audiences.
  • Be energized by building a function from the ground up with new tooling, and act with urgency and precision when a practice or a member is waiting on an answer.

Benefits

  • Medical Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Short & Long Term Disability
  • Life Insurance
  • 401k with company match
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid Parental Leave

Compensation: Base salary range: $260,000 to $280,000 plus bonus potential depending on relevant experience, location, and qualifications.

About You:

  • You use LOGIC in your decision making and understand that progress is critical to making change. You focus on the execution of your content while balancing a fast-paced environment and you take the time to celebrate both the small & big wins.
  • INCLUSION is a core tenant of your personal beliefs. A diverse and inclusive environment is incredibly important to you. You understand and desire to be a part of a diverse team with different experiences and perspectives & you cherish the differences in each individual that you interact with.
  • You have the GRIT, drive and ambition to tackle big problems. Big problems require big ideas and a team that supports new ideas.
  • You care deeply for your customers are driven to keep HUMANITY in all decisions. Your customers aren’t just the individuals using your product. They are the driving factor in your motivation to make a change.
  • Integrity guides you in life. Focusing on the TRUTH vs. giving people the answers they want to hear.
  • You thrive in a Team Environment. Collaboration is key in innovation and creating change.

These pillars of LIGHT are a reminder to our team that we are making a difference by providing guidance and support in navigating the often complex and confusing landscape of healthcare. We hope that through this LIGHT, individuals can find their way to the best care, resources, and support they need to get back to life.

If this sounds like you, we would love to connect to speak further about career opportunities at Lantern.

Please apply to our role & someone from our Talent Acquisition Team will reach out to help you navigate our interview process.

The Senior Managing Accident Reconstructionist leads a team of expert staff in reconstructing vehicular accidents and requires excessive experience in forensic engineering and/or accident reconstruction investigations. This role requires traveling to the site of vehicular accidents, assessing conditions leading to the accident, utilizing specialized software to reconstruct the accidents, working with forensic animators to develop 3D models and other graphics for trial exhibits, accurately analyzing crash patterns, and providing written conclusions to determine factors contributing to the accidents. The ideal candidate has an established network of clientele and is experienced with building, establishing, and maintaining rapport with this network. This is a fully remote role open to candidates located anywhere in the United States. Candidates located in the listed states are encouraged to apply.

In This Role, You Will:

Lead a team of experts in conducting accident investigations by traveling to and documenting accident scenes, downloading vehicle data recorders, performing analysis of accidents using crash simulation software, writing reports as needed and providing litigation support services to clients. Handle large, complex projects and manage all aspects of the project from start to finish. Support business development efforts by building and maintaining rapport with current clients and generating new work for themselves and a team of experts supporting them. Partner with business development representatives, attend conferences and events to promote the company and skills of expert staff. Communicate with clients and team regarding scope of work, investigation tasks, budget, and ensures all project completion timelines, deadlines and deliverables are met. Provide expert testimony in depositions or trials as expert witness if/when requested. Analyze vehicle crush patterns and conducts research (vehicle specifications, crash test data, maintenance history, etc.) Process 3D laser scan point cloud data using engineering workstation computers. Work with forensic animators to develop scaled 3D drawings of crash scenes and vehicles. Utilize PC Crash (or other similar collision reconstruction software) to perform simulations of automobile collisions. Utilize engineering principles and momentum equations to calculate factors such as impact and departure speeds, collision forces, trajectories of the vehicles, and other types of analysis. Compare calculations with crash test reports of similar collisions to correlate damages based on speed and velocity. Create reports as requested by clients detailing the accident reconstruction process and including findings and conclusions. Provide reports to clients to assist with determining the contributory factors of an accident. Act as a team lead and review other staff's work to ensure project deliverables are accurate and timely. Research papers and journals related to vehicular accident reconstruction to advance the scientific techniques used in the reconstruction work.

jobs.description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?

Leidos is a Fortune 500® company with nearly $18B in sales and 50,000 employees that brings over 70 years of experience in support of both investor-owned and municipal utility growth goals. Leidos Energy helps utilities address complex challenges through comprehensive, performance-based solutions delivered across the full project lifecycle. Our capabilities include engineering, planning, project management, construction management, and commissioning services for electric power substations, transmission and distribution systems, protection and controls design, and electrification programs. Utilities nationwide rely on Leidos for trusted power industry expertise, demonstrated by our work with more than 75 investor-owned utilities and over 100 municipal and cooperative utilities, as well as a growing portfolio of private developer clients.

Your greatest work is ahead!

Leidos Energy is seeking a Wind Energy Technical Advisor to support Owner's Advisory and Lender's Technical Advisory engagements across onshore and offshore wind projects. You will assess wind turbine technology with a focus on blades and project risk on behalf of developers, owners, investors, and financial institutions. This role pairs deep composites and blade expertise with a strong command of wind turbine systems, and requires clear, defensible technical reporting that supports investment and financing decisions.

Location: Ideal candidate may be remote in the United States or Canada. Main offices are in Framingham/Boston MA, Denver CO, and Greenville, SC for those seeking an office/hybrid environment.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead or support technical due diligence for wind projects on behalf of lenders, equity investors, and owners, covering technology, design, construction, and operations.
  • Evaluate wind turbine technology and OEM track record, with a primary focus on wind turbine blades but also including drivetrain, generator, converter, pitch and yaw systems, controls, towers, and foundations.
  • Assess blade design, manufacturing quality, and field performance, including structural design, layup and bonding, leading-edge erosion, lightning protection, and fatigue life.
  • Review blade damage, repair methodologies, and composite repair procedures (e.g., laminate, adhesive, and coating repairs), and judge long-term effectiveness and cost implications.
  • Analyze failure modes, serial defects, warranty claims, and root-cause findings, and translate them into risk ratings and financial sensitivities.
  • Review wind turbine supply, installation, and service agreements, including warranty terms, availability guarantees, and long-term service agreement (LTSA) provisions, from a technical perspective.
  • Performing independent engineering reviews and preparing reports for financing, root cause analysis, expert witness, etc.
  • Support owner's engineering activities such as OEM selection, factory and site inspections, commissioning oversight, acceptance testing, and end-of-warranty inspections.
  • Evaluate operating and maintenance strategies, spare parts planning, major component replacement forecasts, and lifetime extension or repowering options.
  • Prepare clear, well-supported technical reports and present findings to clients, lenders, and project stakeholders.
  • Contribute to proposals, scopes of work, budgets, and business development.

What does Leidos need from me?

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical or related field with five plus years of experience in wind energy.
  • Previous work experience with an independent engineer, developer, wind turbine manufacturer, engineering firm, EPC firm, and/or a wind consultancy.
  • Flexibility to work across wind turbine subsystems and other energy generating technologies.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership in topics related to wind technology and wind systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to summarize complex analyses and topics both in written reports and verbally.
  • Understanding of industry trends in wind turbine and composite technology, analysis methods, and project optimization.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform under pressure both verbally and in writing with a diverse set of clients to include private equity, infrastructure, hedge funds, investment, commercial banks, private developers, legal and financial advisors, original equipment manufacturers, and energy service companies.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform independently and as a team, and to collaborate on complex, multi-disciplinary tasks.
  • Effectively and independently prioritize multiple tasks and schedules.
  • Demonstrated ability to “think outside the box” to develop analysis methods and opinions which meet the unique needs of the client (internal and external).

Favorable if you have:

  • Experience performing independent engineering/consulting services in the wind industry.
  • Understanding of advanced and emerging composite technologies, wind turbine systems, and component loading.
  • Understanding wind turbine suitability, including design/certification and site-specific considerations
  • Understanding of the IEC 61400 standards in the wind industry.
  • Experience with wind turbine blade manufacturing processes including quality systems and audits.
  • Experience climbing wind turbines and holding relevant certification(s).
  • Experience performing independent reviews of wind resource and energy production assessments and associated written reports produced by third parties;
  • Experience developing scopes of work and budgets with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Experience managing projects and clients.

jobs.description:
Be the one building AI-powered experiences where they matter most.

At Genesys, we help organizations create better customer experiences through AI-powered experience orchestration. Our platform connects people, systems, data and AI to help organizations deliver more personalized service, improve operational efficiency and build stronger customer relationships.

Help build, support and operate technology used by more than 8,000 organizations in over 100 countries – moving AI from possibility to production in real-world enterprise environments every day.


Job Title: Senior Manager, Learning & Enablement

Location: U.S. (remote) - This role may be based in any U.S. time zone. Because the team is globally distributed, regular availability between 6:00-8:00am Pacific Time is required to support EMEA and APAC collaboration.

Department: HR - Talent Development

Reports To: Director of Learning & Enablement


Overview

The Senior Manager, Learning & Enablement leads a small, global team that designs, builds, and delivers learning and capability-building solutions across the business. The role covers enterprise-wide, function-agnostic learning, with occasional support for smaller functions that don’t have dedicated enablement of their own. To be clear on scope, this isn’t a go-to-market or sales enablement role: Genesys has dedicated enablement teams supporting major functions like Product, Sales, and Customer Success.


It’s a hands-on, player-coach role for someone who wants to work alongside a small team rather than set top-down strategy for how learning works across the company. A central part of the role is exploring how AI can actually change the learning experience, things like adaptive paths, simulation-based practice, or AI coaching, tested in small, practical ways. It also means helping instructional designers rethink their own roles as AI takes on more of the production work.


This person approaches the learning experience the way a product manager approaches a product: starting with what the learner needs and how it feels to use, not just whether it follows established learning design theory.


Key Responsibilities


Team Leadership & Capability Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop a small global team of instructional designers and learning specialists, setting clear priorities and building a culture of experimentation and accountability.
  • Help the team build new skills as roles and tools evolve, with a focus on judgment, curation, and experience design as AI takes on more of the production work.

Designing the Learning Experience Like a Product

  • Start from what a genuinely good experience looks like for the learner, then figure out how AI and our existing tools can get there.
  • Make the most of the AI and learning tools we already have, looking for new features or approaches that move us toward more personalized or adaptive learning.
  • When new tools emerge for consideration, bring a grounded point of view on whether it adds real value beyond what we already have, partnering with our technical lead and IT as needed.
  • Think through the governance questions that come with AI-generated content, like who can create, who can publish, and how quality gets checked.

Evolving How the Team Works

  • Look at the team's process, from intake through delivery, and figure out with the team where AI or simpler changes can help, without over-engineering a small function.

Enterprise Partnership in a Federated Model

  • Proactively build relationships with practitioners and leaders across the learning and enablement ecosystem to align on design approaches, asset reuse, and ways to reduce duplicated effort, even without formal authority to do so.
  • Build leverage without growing the team by creating things like a facilitator network or self-service tools, especially within HR, to extend the team's reach beyond what it can deliver directly.

Transformation & Functional Enablement Support (Secondary)

  • Provide selective enablement support for broader transformation or functional initiatives, in partnership with Transformation, Change Management, HR, and functional leaders.

Experience

  • 8+ years in Learning and Development, Talent Development, Organizational Development, or similar, with experience changing how learning works, not just producing it.
  • 2+ years managing people, ideally a small, distributed team of learning or talent professionals.
  • Experience using AI to meaningfully change how a team’s work gets done, whether that’s your own team or one you influenced, not just personal productivity habits.
  • Experience evaluating or piloting new AI learning technology, including thinking through value, quality risk, and fit with existing tools.
  • Basic grounding in learning design and adult learning principles, with your real focus on how the learner experiences things.
  • Experience contributing to process improvement or workflow change, inside or outside L&D.

Who You Are and What You've Done

  • You think about the learning experience the way a good product manager thinks about a product: you start with the user and adjust based on real feedback.
  • You're genuinely curious about how AI can change what a learning experience is, and you want to try things, not just discuss them. You can spot what's useful versus what just sounds impressive.
  • You are comfortable operating in ambiguity and “in the gray.” You don't need a fully defined playbook or delivery model to move forward. As AI and agentic experiences change how learning is designed and delivered, you can form a point of view, test it, learn quickly, and adjust the approach as the business need evolves.
  • You care about L&D enough to do it well, but it's not your identity. You're here to help a small team figure out an open problem, not to be an L&D expert or Instructional Design purist.
  • You're comfortable with and genuinely enjoy a role and team that frequently change shape.
  • You've helped people change how they work, balancing accountability with room to experiment.
  • You’re as comfortable being the face of the work as you are doing the work itself. People across levels trust you, and you show up with presence, not just expertise.


Additional Qualifications That Set You Apart

  • Experience in a high-growth SaaS or AI-driven technology company.
  • Hands-on experience with AI-native learning platforms, adaptive learning, or AI coaching.
  • Experience in a lean, resource-constrained team making practical trade-offs.
  • An instructional design or L&D background combined with genuine interest in product thinking.
  • Experience in an actual product role, especially in the HR technology space.

Compensation:

This role has a market-competitive salary with an anticipated base compensation range listed below. Actual salaries will vary depending on a candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and location. This role might also be eligible for a commission or performance-based bonus opportunities.

$133,500.00 - $234,900.00

Position Summary

The INFOR Time & Attendance Application Support /Project Coordinator provides day-to-day support, administration, and troubleshooting for the INFOR Time & Attendance system. This role ensures accurate employee time capture, schedule management, and seamless data flow to payroll. The coordinator serves as the first point of contact for system users, assisting with technical issues, process questions, and training needs. Working closely with HR, Payroll, IT, and Operations, the coordinator helps maintain data integrity, compliance, and system efficiency.

Additionally plays a key role in the successful rollout of the INFOR Time & Attendance system. This role contributes to system configuration, testing, training, data migration, and end-user adoption. Team members collaborate with HR, Payroll, IT, Operations, and external vendors to ensure the application is implemented on time, within scope, and aligned with organizational requirements.

Key Responsibilities

System Support & Administration

  • Act as the first line of support for INFOR Time & Attendance users (employees, managers, HR, payroll).

  • Support system configuration (shift patterns, pay rules, leave types, accruals, schedules).

User Support & Training

  • Provide timely assistance to end-users via email, ticketing system, or phone.

  • Create and maintain user documentation, quick reference guides, and FAQs.

  • Deliver training sessions for employees and managers on system functionality.

jobs.excerpt: NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do.
jobs.description:
NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do. Now, generative AI is opening new possibilities for how people learn, create, and tackle problems. Realizing that potential means answering some of the hardest questions in AI: Where do models fall short? Which risks are we missing? How do we know our safeguards are working? As an expert in machine learning for Evaluations, you’ll help establish the evidence that guides the next generation of safer AI. Your curiosity and scientific judgment can shape what we test, what we learn, and what we build next.


We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer / AI Researcher / Data Scientist to join our AI Safety and Responsibility efforts within Enterprise Risk Management. Engaging directly in engineering tasks, you will apply your data science and statistics skills. You will turn open research questions into rigorous benchmarks, inventive experiments, and tools that reveal how multimodal large language models behave under pressure. Working with researchers and platform engineers, you’ll connect those discoveries to better training methods and safeguards, with reproducible results that inform technical reviews and executive decisions. If you love asking the question no one has thought to test, and building a convincing way to answer it, come help us define what progress in AI safety looks like.


What You Will Be Doing:

  • Safety Benchmarking: Design and maintain safety benchmarks for large language and multimodal models, translating risk scenarios into test cases, datasets, and scoring rubrics.
  • Evaluation Methodology: Define metrics and protocols that assess safety alongside model usefulness, using baselines, uncertainty estimates, and failure analysis to distinguish meaningful improvements from noise.
  • Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases.
  • Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment.
  • Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues.
  • Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers.

What We Need To See:

  • Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 6+ years in the field of machine learning engineering or evaluation.
  • Evaluation Design: Experience developing benchmarks, metrics, and statistically sound comparisons for ML systems, including selecting baselines and interpreting uncertainty. Ability to translate ambiguous evaluation questions into testable experiments.
  • Engineering: Strong Python skills and experience building maintainable shared tools, data pipelines, and experiment-tracking workflows.
  • Analytical Rigor: Ability to assess dataset quality, identify limitations in metrics and scoring methods, and support conclusions with reproducible evidence.
  • Communication: Clearly explain findings and tradeoffs to researchers, engineering partners, and executives.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Evaluation: Experience evaluating LLMs, multimodal models, or agentic systems through adversarial testing or automated red-teaming.
  • Community Contributions: Contributions to public benchmarks or evaluation frameworks.
  • Research Publications: A publication track record and interest in continuing to publish at top tier venues.
  • Human-Aligned Evaluation: Experience validating model-based evaluators against human judgments or designing human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows.
  • Statistical Rigor: Strong model evaluation skills and a commitment to sound statistical practices, including confidence intervals.
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4; and 224,000 USD – 356,500 USD for Level 5.

The Senior Program Manager is responsible for leading and overseeing complex programs composed of multiple, interrelated projects to ensure delivery aligns with strategic business objectives, service commitments, and contractual obligations. We’re looking for an exceptional Senior Manager, Executive Communications to serve as a strategic communications partner to Cisco’s Chief Learning & Future Readiness Officer.

You’ll work closely with leaders across Cisco Learning, corporate communications, and the broader 3P organization to connect business priorities with stories that inform, engage, and inspire.

This role requires more than excellent writing. We’re looking for a strategic thinker, creative storyteller, and trusted advisor who brings sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and the confidence to work with senior executives.

What You’ll Do

Executive Communications Strategy and Counsel

  • Serve as a strategic communications partner to the Chief Learning & Future Readiness Officer, providing thoughtful counsel and recommendations on executive messaging, positioning, and engagement.
  • Develop and execute an integrated executive communications strategy aligned to Cisco Learning’s business priorities and Cisco’s broader corporate narrative.
  • Anticipate communications needs, identify opportunities, and help translate complex business priorities into clear, compelling messages.

Storytelling and Content Development

  • Translate complex topics, including AI, learning innovation, digital skills, and workforce transformation, into accessible and engaging stories.
  • Bring creativity, editorial rigor, and strong attention to detail to every deliverable.

External Thought Leadership and Visibility

  • Help develop and execute a thought leadership strategy that positions Cisco Learning leaders as influential voices in conversations about AI, education, skilling, and the future of work.
  • Prepare executive content and briefing materials for industry conferences, speaking engagements, media opportunities, and strategic stakeholder meetings.
  • Collaborate with public relations, analyst relations, social media, and events teams to identify opportunities that advance Cisco’s business priorities.
  • Stay informed about industry developments and emerging issues to recommend timely, relevant communications opportunities.

Internal Communications

  • Lead communications planning and content development for executive town halls, leadership meetings, organizational announcements, and employee engagement.
  • Partner with Cisco Learning leaders to communicate strategy, business progress, organizational priorities, and transformation initiatives.
  • Help employees understand how their work connects to Cisco’s broader strategy and the future of learning.
  • Support communications during periods of organizational change, bringing clarity, transparency, and consistency to executive messaging.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Execution

  • Partner with communications colleagues across 3P and Cisco to align executive messaging, business priorities, and strategic narratives.
  • Independently manage multiple high-visibility communications projects, often with competing deadlines and evolving requirements.
  • Develop strong working relationships with executive stakeholders and their teams.
  • Use audience insights, engagement data, and feedback to evaluate and improve communications effectiveness.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in executive communications, corporate communications, public relations, journalism, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting senior executives and developing high-quality executive communications.
  • Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills across a variety of formats and audiences.
  • Experience developing and executing strategic communications plans.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate and influence across functions and organizational levels.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in education, learning and development, higher education, digital skilling, workforce development, or related fields is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting C-suite executives or senior leaders within a global technology company or similarly complex organization.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop executive thought leadership and support high-profile external speaking engagements.
  • Strong understanding of AI and emerging technologies, particularly their implications for learning, work, and business transformation.
  • Advanced proficiency with generative AI tools, including practical experience using AI to support research, content development, creative ideation, and communications workflows.
  • Experience developing executive social media strategies and content, particularly for LinkedIn.
  • Strong executive presence, sound business judgment, and the ability to provide candid, constructive counsel to senior stakeholders.
  • Experience working in a global, highly matrixed organization.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

jobs.title: Digital Assets Security Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Who We Are: Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

We are seeking a Digital Assets Security Engineer to own security for Alpaca's crypto and tokenization products. The scope includes custody and key management, transaction authorization policies, secure engineering for wallets and tokenization, and monitoring of high-risk asset movements.

Several of the largest digital asset thefts in recent years started with a compromised signer, a manipulated signing screen, or social engineering of the people who approve transactions. This role focuses on those paths: who can move assets, under what policy, and what approvers see before they sign. You will work in both the engineering details and the governance around them.

This role reports to the CISO and works closely with the crypto and tokenization engineering teams, Crypto Operations, Compliance, GRC, and the wider Security team.

The Security Team is 100% distributed and remote.

Things You Get To Do:

The core responsibilities of the Digital Assets Security Engineer are focused on custody and key security, transaction authorization and governance, secure engineering for crypto and tokenization, and monitoring and response.

Custody and Key Security:

  • Custody Architecture: Own the security design of wallets, vaults, and signing infrastructure across hot, warm, and cold storage, including MPC and HSM configuration.
  • Key Lifecycle: Set requirements for key generation, backup, recovery, rotation, and destruction. Run or oversee key ceremonies and recovery tests with Crypto Operations.
  • Signing Integrity: Secure the path from a transaction request to a signature, including API credentials, co-signers, approval devices, and what approvers see before they sign.

Transaction Authorization and Governance:

  • Transaction Policies: Review transaction authorization policies, such as Fireblocks TAP, including approval quorums, amount thresholds, destination allowlists, and velocity limits. Recommend changes to Crypto Operations and Compliance, who own and approve them.
  • Change Control: Advise on how changes to policies, admins, signers, and allowlisted addresses are proposed, approved, and applied. Confirm every change leaves a reviewable record.
  • Access Reviews: Review admin, signer, approver, and API user access on custody platforms on a set schedule, and flag access that is no longer needed for removal.
  • Third-Party Risk: Assess custody providers, node and RPC providers, token issuers, and other digital asset vendors with Cyber GRC.
  • Standards and Evidence: In collaboration with the Cyber GRC team, write the security standards for digital asset operations, and provide technical evidence for audits and regulatory exams.

Secure Engineering for Crypto and Tokenization:

  • Design Reviews: Review architecture and code changes for wallet services, custody integrations, blockchain node infrastructure, and tokenization flows. Give engineers clear, practical requirements.
  • Threat Modeling: Threat model minting, redemption, transfers, settlement, and reconciliation between on-chain balances and internal books and records.
  • Smart Contract Review: Review token contracts and issuer controls, such as mint and burn authority, upgradeability, admin keys, and freeze functions, for tokens we support or integrate with.
  • Service Identity and Secrets: Set requirements for how services authenticate to custody platforms, including HSM-backed signing keys, scoped API credentials, and least-privilege service accounts.

Monitoring and Response:

  • Detection: Define alerts for high-risk activity, such as policy and admin changes, new destination addresses, unusual withdrawals, and signer changes. Work with Security Operations to build and tune them.
  • On-Chain Monitoring: Monitor the addresses and contracts Alpaca depends on for suspicious activity, with Security Operations and Compliance.
  • Incident Response: Lead the digital asset side of security incidents, including suspected key compromise, unauthorized transfers, and malicious approvals. Maintain playbooks to freeze, rotate, and recover.
  • On-Call: Participate in the Security on-call rotation after onboarding and cross-training.

Who You Are (Must-Haves):

  • Excited about Alpaca's mission and what we're building
  • 5+ years of experience in security engineering, including 2+ years securing digital asset, crypto, or blockchain systems
  • Hands-on experience with institutional custody, such as MPC or HSM-backed wallets, key backup and recovery, and policy-based transaction controls (Fireblocks,Turnkey, BitGo, Copper, or similar)
  • Experience designing or reviewing transaction authorization policies, including approval quorums, amount thresholds, address allowlists, and separation of initiators, approvers, and signers
  • Working knowledge of how transactions and signatures work on EVM chains and Solana, including token standards, token approvals, nonces, and finality
  • A clear understanding of how digital asset theft happens in practice: signer device compromise, blind signing, social engineering of operators, address poisoning, malicious token approvals, and key exfiltration
  • Able to read code and design documents well enough to challenge implementation choices, with programming experience in Python, Go, TypeScript, Rust, or similar
  • Experience with cloud security, service identity, secrets management, and KMS or HSM
  • Experience writing security standards and producing control evidence for auditors or regulators
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially when explaining risk to engineers, operators, and compliance partners
  • Willing to participate in an on-call rotation

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves):

  • Experience securing broker-dealers, exchanges, custodians, money services businesses, or other regulated financial platforms
  • Smart contract security review experience (Solidity or Rust) with tools such as Foundry, Slither, or Echidna
  • Experience with tokenized securities, stablecoins, or on-chain settlement and reconciliation
  • Experience running key ceremonies or designing custody recovery and disaster recovery procedures
  • Experience with blockchain analytics and on-chain monitoring tools
  • Ability to balance security rigor with operational efficiency and business needs

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager - Banking & Payments
jobs.excerpt: In 1933, Harry Beck introduced a radically different map of the London Underground.
jobs.description:
In 1933, Harry Beck introduced a radically different map of the London Underground. Rather than faithfully depicting the geography of London, he simplified the sprawling transit network into clean lines, clear connections, and a system that anyone could navigate. Distances were distorted, angles were standardized, and unnecessary details disappeared. The result was something far more useful than a geographically accurate map: a way for millions of people to understand a complex system and confidently find their way through it.

Beck understood something fundamental. The best way to explain something complicated isn't to show people everything. It's to understand what matters to them and make that unmistakably clear.

At Mercury, we believe great product marketing works the same way. Banking* and payments can be complex, but the value they create for customers shouldn't be. Our job is to understand what people need, find the essence of what we're building, and help customers see how it can make their lives better.

We're a financial technology company building products that help ambitious businesses do more with their money. From everyday banking and payments to international money movement and emerging capabilities like agentic payments, we're making complex financial workflows feel remarkably simple.

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to help bring these products to market, communicate their value, and make sure customers discover and use what we're building.

This role sits at the intersection of Product, Marketing, and Revenue. You'll develop positioning, lead go-to-market strategies, drive successful product launches, and identify opportunities to increase adoption and revenue.

We care deeply about craft, but successful product marketing is about more than a beautiful campaign or a well-executed announcement. It's about understanding customers, building an effective plan, and driving meaningful results.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

In this role, you'll:

  • Lead impactful product launches. Own end-to-end go-to-market strategy and execution for new banking and payments capabilities, including emerging agentic features. Develop launch plans, align cross-functional teams, prepare customer-facing partners, and measure impact on product adoption and business goals.
  • Get close to our customers. Build a deep understanding of how founders and finance teams manage money, what challenges they face, and why they choose one financial product over another. Turn these insights into compelling positioning, messaging, and GTM strategies.
  • Execute AI-first. Use AI to work smarter, move faster, and produce better outcomes. You’ll build and use existing workflows, automations, and repeatable processes that improve how you approach research, launch execution, competitive intelligence, and other core responsibilities.
  • Help more customers discover and use Mercury. Partner with Product, Lifecycle, Activation, and Revenue to drive adoption of banking and payments capabilities. Identify growth opportunities, test hypotheses, and improve product usage over time.
  • Become an expert on our market. Develop a sharp understanding of the banking and payments competitive landscape, including emerging fintech products and traditional financial institutions. Translate market insights into differentiated positioning and actionable recommendations.
  • Equip our Revenue teams to win. Build trusted relationships with customer-facing teams and develop the competitive intelligence, battlecards, messaging, and training they need to communicate Mercury's value confidently and accurately.
  • Work with exceptional cross-functional partners. Collaborate with Product, Brand, Creative, Lifecycle, and Revenue to bring go-to-market strategies to life. Help shape strong campaign briefs and channel strategies, drawing on specialized creative expertise when needed.
  • Connect marketing to business impact. Define clear objectives for launches and growth initiatives, track meaningful performance indicators, and communicate what worked, what didn't, and what we should do next.
  • Own the full picture. Manage multiple projects and product areas simultaneously, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and prioritize the work that will have the greatest impact on Mercury and its customers.

  • Know how to build a complete GTM strategy, from customer insight and positioning through launch execution, field readiness, and post-launch measurement.

  • Can translate complex products and capabilities into clear, compelling messaging.
  • Understand that great product marketing extends beyond launches into product adoption, competitive positioning, and revenue growth.
  • Are comfortable using customer feedback, data, and experimentation to evaluate and improve marketing performance.
  • Enjoy working closely with Product, Marketing, and Revenue teams and know how to build trusted relationships across functions.
  • Can manage several competing priorities, make good decisions with incomplete information, and independently move important work forward.
  • Experience in fintech, banking*, or payments is a plus, but it's not required. We're equally interested in people who have done exceptional work in other B2B industries and are excited to learn something new.

Role Title: Principal Research Scientist (Computer Science / Computational Physics)

Role Type: Contractor (flexible, Part-Time or Full-Time)

micro1 is engaging Principal Research Scientist (Computer Science / Computational Physics)s to contribute to an advanced customer project at the intersection of computational theory and AI. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. You will work with frontier AI models and agents to tackle open problems, drive research direction, and define standards for scientific breakthroughs. Your insights and rigorous approach will be pivotal in charting what counts as genuine progress within your subfield.

Scope of Work

  1. Identify, frame, and articulate foundational open problems, theoretical bounds, or simulation challenges where verifiable progress can be demonstrated.
  2. Guide AI models and agents in multi-step research processes—ranging from proofs and algorithms to numerical experiments and high-performance simulations.
  3. Critically assess and validate results, utilizing proof checks, computational reproduction, and formal methods to pinpoint the limits of model-generated reasoning.
  4. Evaluate and document the novelty, correctness, and significance of research outputs relative to current literature and established results.
  5. Produce clear, concise research memos detailing research attempts, partial solutions, and observed model limitations or failure patterns.
  6. Advise on research directions, recommending promising subfields and open problems suitable for advancement via AI models and computational tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. 7 - 10+ years of active research in computer science or mathematical/computational physics, with a strong record of scholarly contributions.
  2. Recognition at the field level—such as major prizes, society fellowships, or plenary/invited talks at top scholarly events.
  3. A consistent publication record in leading venues within your domain, with recent results published in the past year.
  4. Demonstrated success resolving named open problems or introducing influential concepts adopted by peers.
  5. Deep, hands-on experience with computational research methods: simulation, numerical analysis, algorithmic implementation, and/or high-performance computing environments.
  6. Proven ability to rigorously examine technical work outside your immediate area of expertise.
  7. Experience on program committees, editorial boards, or with formal research tools (e.g., Lean, Coq, SAT/SMT solvers) is a strong plus, as is a public record of outlining open problems or showcasing research with advanced AI systems.

Tradewater is on a mission to bend the curve on global warming as quickly as possible, directly combating climate change by identifying, collecting, and mitigating the release of non-CO₂ superpollutants—including old refrigerants, excess halons, and methane. These actions reduce potent greenhouse gases, protect the ozone layer, and generate high-integrity carbon credits that fund and expand our mission worldwide. Our projects also create measurable social and economic value for local communities, creating long-lasting benefits that strengthen economies and improve ecosystems endangering public health.

Targeting superpollutants offers one of the fastest, most cost-effective climate strategies available today. These non-CO₂ gases drive nearly half of all human-caused warming, are exponentially more potent than CO₂, and cannot be removed from the atmosphere once released. Cutting halocarbons and methane delivers bigger and faster climate benefits than CO₂ reductions alone and leading models, from MIT to the IPCC, agree that tackling superpollutants is essential to any credible net-zero pathway. Since 2012, Tradewater has prevented over 12.4 million tons of CO₂ equivalent from releasing into the atmosphere and are on path to prevent at least 30 million tons by 2030. We are committed to bending the curve on global warming as quickly as possible and delivering trusted, measurable, scalable climate impact today.

jobs.description:
The Program Director owns the execution and delivery integrity of Sapiens customer programs. This role sits within the Delivery Success team and is the primary accountable leader for program governance, milestone management, and value delivery inside a customer engagement.

The role is accountable for ensuring that every milestone is delivered to agreed exit criteria, that every risk is visible before it becomes a crisis, and that the delivery model operates at the pace that shortens time-to-value for the customer.

The Program Director operates an AI-native delivery model in which the execution layer is progressively automated, enabling the role to focus on discernment, governance, and the customer relationship. The role works in close partnership with the Customer Success team, together stewarding the Customer Value Journey – the end-to-end path from implementation through to long-term success and value realization. Commercial outcomes – NRR, ARR, account margin, and customer referenceability – are shared responsibilities.

Job Responsibilities

Program Delivery & Commercial Outcomes:
  • End-to-end delivery ownership: Leads the full program lifecycle from initiation through planning, execution, and closure. Accountable for delivery on time, within scope, and within budget across all workstreams – including platform implementation, integration, data migration, and business change.
  • Time to Value: Owns the pace at which the customer realizes measurable business outcomes from the Sapiens engagement. Defines the time-to-value baseline at program initiation, tracks progress at every milestone, and uses delivery decisions to actively shorten it.
  • AI-led SaaS implementation velocity: Moves programs toward faster implementation cycles consistent with Sapiens’ AI-led SaaS delivery model, applying configuration-over-customization discipline.
  • Commercial Outcomes: In partnership with Customer Success, owns NRR contribution of the customer portfolio, drives expansion levers, and reports against them.
  • Growth: Identifies upsell and cross-sell potential during delivery and converts insight into pipeline opportunities.
  • AI-native execution model: Operates a delivery model in which AI supports execution activities such as status tracking, risk summarization, documentation, and reporting cadence.

Milestone Management & Exit Criteria:
  • Milestone ownership: Defines, manages, and tracks program milestones with clear definitions of done, agreed exit criteria, and formal customer acceptance.
  • Exit criteria discipline: Works with the customer to agree exit criteria at the start of each phase; manages scope through change orders aligned to those criteria.
  • Milestone-based billing alignment: Ensures delivery milestones align with billing triggers and commercial events.
  • Risk and dependency management: Maintains a live program risk register, manages interdependencies across teams, and drives resolution proactively.

Insurance Industry Fluency & Customer Understanding:
  • Insurance domain depth: Develops deep understanding of the customer’s business, operating model, and regulatory environment.
  • Customer relationship ownership: Holds the customer relationship at the program level, including C-suite engagement and trust-based partnership.

Proactive Customer Relationship & Escalation Management:
  • Customer relationship ownership at the program level: Holds the customer relationship at the C-suite level on substance and trust. Is the person the customer calls when something genuinely matters.
  • Proactive escalation management: Anticipates delivery risks and customer concerns, addressing issues before they escalate.
  • Customer Success partnership: Works in close coordination with the Customer Success Manager on the account. The PDCA owns delivery execution; the CS team owns the commercial relationship and expansion trajectory. Together, the PDCA and CS team own the Customer Value Journey – the handoff between these functions is deliberate, documented, and clean. Customer health is a shared metric.

Resource Orchestration & Team Leadership:

  • Team leadership and development: Treats team development as a commercial lever, not an HR task – holding growth conversations early and building capability with intention. Leads the full talent lifecycle with candor and integrity, from onboarding through to role transitions.
  • Sapiens ambassadorship: Carries the Sapiens point of view into customer environments. Knows the Insurance Ontology argument, the AutonomousInsurer thesis, and the AI moat – and can hold them in a room.
  • Project Manager leadership: Directly leads a team of Project Managers across the program. Sets standards, drives accountability, and develops PM capability with intention. The PDCA is the delivery standard-setter on the account – the team performs to the level the PDCA models and demands.

Job Requirements

  • 15+ years of experience leading complex enterprise software programs, including at least 5 years in senior delivery leadership roles.
  • Deep insurance domain knowledge (Life & Pension, Property & Casualty, or equivalent specialty lines), with familiarity in insurance technology platforms.
  • Demonstrated expertise in milestone-based delivery governance, exit criteria design, scope control, and change management.
  • Experience leading global cross-functional teams, including SI partners and offshore delivery resources.
  • AI transformation experience, including use of AI tools across program management and delivery.
  • Strong program financial management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, and cost-to-serve awareness.
