jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (AI Driven) - Curveglass
jobs.excerpt: Curveglass is a startup incubated by AE Studio that provides a flight-level correction layer for airline revenue management, helping airlines make better decisions through advanced data science and modeling.
jobs.description:
Curveglass is a startup incubated by AE Studio that provides a flight-level correction layer for airline revenue management, helping airlines make better decisions through advanced data science and modeling.

As part of the AE Studio ecosystem, Curveglass combines the speed, focus, and ownership of a startup with access to a broader network of engineering, AI, and product expertise.

Curveglass runs directly inside each airline’s cloud environment. Our architecture consists of a shared Core, which contains the models and is maintained by the core team, and a client-specific Adapter, which handles everything needed to make Curveglass work within each airline’s environment — including the web application, APIs, data integrations, business rules, and exports into the airline’s systems.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer at Curveglass, you’ll own the technical implementation of Curveglass for one or two airline clients end-to-end.

This is a hands-on engineering role with broad ownership. You’ll build and maintain client-specific Adapter code, work across frontend and backend systems, integrate with airline data and infrastructure, and deploy and operate Curveglass within client cloud environments.

You’ll also work directly with clients. That means understanding their technical and business needs, participating in and leading meetings, troubleshooting issues, analyzing recommendation results in collaboration with revenue management teams, and managing technical expectations as needed.

You’ll work closely with the Curveglass core team to determine what should be solved within a client’s Adapter and what should become part of the shared Core. You’ll bring client needs back to the team as roadmap input and Core change requests, while owning the implementation of client-specific functionality yourself.

We’re looking for someone who enjoys the full lifecycle of software engineering: understanding the problem, building the solution, deploying it, and seeing how it performs in the real world.

You’ll have meaningful ownership over the systems you build and the opportunity to influence Curveglass’s architecture and product as we grow.

If you enjoy owning technical problems end-to-end and working closely with the people using what you build, we’d love to talk.

ABOUT YOU

You’re a strong, pragmatic Software Engineer who enjoys owning systems beyond just writing the code.

You’re comfortable working across different parts of the stack and taking responsibility for an implementation from beginning to end: understanding requirements, designing the solution, building integrations and product functionality, deploying infrastructure, troubleshooting issues, and continuing to improve the system once it’s live.

You’re comfortable operating in a startup environment where problems may not always come neatly defined. You can take ownership, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and move from an ambiguous problem to a reliable production solution.

You also communicate well with people outside of engineering. You can understand the business context behind a technical request, explain technical decisions clearly, and lead conversations with clients when needed.

You work well independently, collaborate closely with data science and product teams, and care about building software that is reliable, maintainable, and genuinely useful.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Strong software engineering experience: You can independently design, build, debug, and maintain production systems.
  • Fluency in Python: You’re highly proficient with Python and comfortable using it in production environments.
  • Full-stack development: You’re comfortable working with TypeScript and React and can own frontend functionality when needed.
  • SQL and data integration: You can work confidently with relational data, APIs, client datasets, and production data flows.
  • Cloud infrastructure: You’re comfortable deploying and maintaining applications in AWS or Azure.
  • Containers and infrastructure as code: You have hands-on experience with containers and tools such as Terraform as part of your regular development workflow.
  • End-to-end ownership: You’re comfortable taking responsibility for a system across application code, integrations, infrastructure, deployment, and ongoing maintenance.
  • Client-facing communication: You’re comfortable interacting directly with clients, leading technical meetings when needed, explaining decisions clearly, managing expectations, and pushing back thoughtfully when appropriate.
  • Business thinking: You care about why something is being built and the outcome it needs to create, not just the technical implementation.
  • Production-minded development: You write maintainable code and care about reliability, observability, debugging, and how systems behave in real-world environments.
  • AI-powered development: You use modern AI coding tools as part of your daily development workflow and know how to use them effectively without sacrificing quality.
  • Self-management: You can take ownership of complex problems, navigate ambiguity, and deliver without constant oversight.
  • Effective communication in English: You’re fluent in spoken and written English and can confidently communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Timezone flexibility: You’re comfortable occasionally adapting meeting hours to work with clients across the Americas, Europe, and the Middle East.

Bonus Points for

  • Enterprise implementation experience: You’ve implemented enterprise or data products where customers require meaningful integration and customization rather than a purely self-service SaaS product.
  • Airline or revenue management experience: Familiarity with airline pricing, forecasting, revenue management, or related systems.
  • Data engineering experience: You’ve worked with production data pipelines and technologies such as Parquet, Snowflake, or similar data infrastructure.
  • Spanish or Portuguese: Professional proficiency in either language.
  • Startup experience: You thrive in fast-moving environments, enjoy ambiguity, and are comfortable taking ownership beyond a narrowly defined job description.
  • Cloud deployment experience: You’ve deployed and operated applications or infrastructure within enterprise AWS or Azure environments.
  • Strong product instincts: You understand when something should be solved as client-specific functionality versus becoming part of a broader product.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Startup ownership, backed by AE Studio: Join a focused, fast-moving startup while benefiting from the broader engineering, AI, and product ecosystem of AE Studio.
  • High-impact engineering: Build production systems that directly shape the Curveglass product and how airlines use it.
  • End-to-end responsibility: Own your work from architecture and implementation through deployment, integration, and ongoing operation.
  • Real-world problems: Work on complex engineering and data problems within airline revenue management, where the software you build directly supports business decisions.
  • Direct product exposure: Work closely with the people using what you build and bring those insights back into technical and product decisions.
  • Product influence: Help shape Curveglass’s architecture, roadmap, and approach to client-specific versus shared product functionality.
  • Small, collaborative team: Work closely with engineering, data science, product, and leadership, with significant autonomy over how you solve problems.
  • Remote-first culture: Work from anywhere, or connect with the broader AE Studio team and community.
  • Flexible schedules: We care about outcomes, ownership, and impact—not micromanagement.
  • Competitive compensation: Competitive pay and the opportunity to grow alongside the company.
  • Opportunities for growth: Help shape how Curveglass approaches engineering, infrastructure, integrations, and technical decision-making as we scale.

jobs.description:
Description

Sprout Social is looking to hire a Business Analyst, GTM Systems to the Sales & Customer Experience team.

You’ll be the bridge between our revenue teams and the systems they run on. You’ll turn business needs into clear requirements, make sure what gets built actually works before it reaches the field, and work hand in hand with our Salesforce IT team. You’ll also play a leading role in our CPQ evaluation and in fixing how we measure marketing and pipeline attribution.

Why join Sprout’s Revenue Operations, Sales & Customer Experience team?

At Sprout Social, our Sales and Customer Experience team is the driving force behind how today’s most innovative brands use Sprout to power the future of customer connection. We sell and support the leading social intelligence platform for businesses, helping organizations unlock the full value of social data to drive strategic decisions. Through powerful social intelligence and trusted partnership, we enable teams to build authentic relationships and drive meaningful business impact.

As the strategic engine of our go-to-market organization, Revenue Operations builds the infrastructure that turns data into action. We specialize in architecting world-class processes and delivering the operational clarity that allows our teams to move with speed, anticipate market shifts, and optimize the entire customer lifecycle for sustainable growth.

In this role, you will collaborate with the brightest minds in the industry to support global giants like Salesforce, Airbnb, and Equifax. Just as importantly, we believe in the power of our people. You’ll find a culture that honors your ambition, encourages you to explore new horizons, and provides the framework for you to build a career that matters. If you’re ready to champion innovation and accelerate your impact, this is where you can do your best work.

What you’ll do

  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Renewals and Deal Desk to turn business needs into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria.
  • Own intake and prioritization for GTM systems requests, working with the Director of GTM Systems & Applied AI and Salesforce IT to maintain a single, prioritized backlog.
  • Plan and run user acceptance testing, triage defects, and secure business-owner sign-off before changes reach the field.
  • Write release notes and field communications, and support reps and managers through changes.
  • Lead requirements, scenario design and scoring for our CPQ evaluation, and support delivery of the CPQ roadmap.
  • Define and fix marketing and pipeline attribution: requirements, source data capture in Salesforce, and validated reporting that Marketing and Sales both trust.
  • Monitor data quality on forecast, renewals and source fields, find root causes, and keep data and process definitions documented.
  • Use AI tools to draft, test and document, and spend your own time on judgment, review and decisions.

What you’ll bring

You know how revenue teams work and how to get the right thing built. You write requirements that engineers can build from, you’re rigorous about testing, and you earn trust with everyone from a frontline rep to a VP.

The minimum qualifications for this role include:

  • 4+ years of experience in business analysis, systems analysis or sales operations, supporting a B2B SaaS go-to-market team.
  • Hands-on Salesforce experience and a working understanding of the data model.
  • Proven ability to gather business requirements and write user stories and acceptance criteria.
  • Experience planning and running UAT and managing releases with a central IT team that owns the platform.
  • Fluency in GTM data: pipeline, forecast, bookings and renewals.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with both frontline teams and executives.

Preferred qualifications for this role include:

  • Experience with Salesforce CPQ or quote-to-cash, or running a systems evaluation or vendor selection.
  • Experience with marketing or pipeline attribution.
  • Experience with Gong or another revenue intelligence platform.
  • Salesforce Administrator certification, or familiarity with SOQL.
  • Experience using AI tools to speed up analysis, documentation and testing.

How you’ll grow

Within 1 month, you’ll plant your roots, including:

  • Complete Sprout Social’s new hire training & onboarding program alongside other new Sprout team members. You’ll gain a broader understanding of our products and how your role fits into the organization.
  • Make a plan with your manager to set initial priorities, align on expectations for your role, plant goalposts for your career, and learn about Sprout’s approach to building and releasing GTM systems changes.
  • Learn our GTM stack, the Salesforce data model and Salesforce IT’s release process.
  • Meet your key stakeholders in Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Renewals and Deal Desk.

Within 3 months, you’ll start hitting your stride by:

  • Build connections with members from other teams through active networking and community building.
  • Run intake and a standing cadence with Salesforce IT, and ship your first release end to end with stories, UAT and field communications.
  • Document the requirements baseline and evaluation criteria for CPQ.
  • Audit current attribution gaps and agree on requirements with Marketing and Sales leadership.

Within 6 months, you’ll be making a clear impact through:

  • Have your first performance conversation with your manager, where you’ll discuss your accomplishments in your role and work together to build goals for your professional growth.
  • Lead the CPQ evaluation, including scenario scripts, demos or proofs of concept, and a scored recommendation.
  • Own UAT for our Gong Forecasting rollout.
  • Agree on attribution definitions and rules, and test the Salesforce changes with IT.

Within 12 months, you’ll make this role your own by:

  • Surprise us! Use your unique ideas and abilities to change your team in beneficial ways that we haven’t even considered yet.
  • Own requirements and UAT for the first waves of the CPQ roadmap and our multiple contracts per account work.
  • Deliver pipeline attribution reporting that Marketing and Sales both accept.
  • Show a clear data quality trend and documented definitions that teams and AI agents can rely on.

Of course what is outlined above is the ideal timeline, but things may shift based on business needs and other projects and tasks could be added at the discretion of your manager.

Our Benefits Program

We’re proud to regularly be recognized for our team, product, and culture. We invest in our team with a comprehensive, competitive benefits program:

  • Comprehensive Health & Wellness: Premium BCBSIL medical, dental (high/low plans), and vision (Eyemed) insurance for you and your eligible dependents.
  • Premium Mental Health Support: Full, free access to Modern Health for you and your dependents, including coaching, therapy sessions, and digital wellness resources.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with a 50% company match on your first 6% of contributions (a 3% total match).
  • Financial Security: 100% employer-paid Life and Disability insurance for your peace of mind.
  • Flexible Paid Time Off: A flexible PTO policy, supplemented with additional company-wide Rest & Recharge days throughout the year.
  • Paid Parental Leave: Up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents to support you in expanding your family.
  • Annual Lifestyle Stipend: A $1,000 USD annual Lifestyle Spending Account to spend on your physical, mental, and financial well-being.
  • Work From Home Support: A one-time $550 USD stipend to set up your home office, plus a monthly $50 USD stipend for internet.
  • Giving Back: 16 hours of paid volunteer time annually, plus a $100 annual match for your charitable donations.
  • Additional Financial Perks: Access to pre-tax commuter benefits, subsidized child/eldercare (Care.com), discounted pet insurance (Figo), and no-cost personalized financial wellness support through Your Money Line.

jobs.title: Senior Talent Acquisition Partner
jobs.excerpt: The Company Versaterm is a PE-backed, high-growth SaaS company building a fully integrated platform across the entire public safety ecosystem — dispatch, law enforcement, forensics, courts, and beyond.
jobs.description:
The Company

Versaterm is a PE-backed, high-growth SaaS company building a fully integrated platform across the entire public safety ecosystem — dispatch, law enforcement, forensics, courts, and beyond. We've grown through strategic acquisitions and deep product investment. What connects all of it is a single purpose: give public safety agencies the tools and insights to make better decisions in high-stakes moments.

When a 911 call is answered, a detective investigates a case, or a forensic lab processes evidence, there's a good chance our software is working behind the scenes. That's been true for over four decades.

AI is central to where we're going. Not as a feature but as core infrastructure. We're embedding intelligence directly into the workflows our customers rely on every day, and we're doing it alongside them. Our customers tell us what the mission demands. We build what answers it.

This work attracts a specific kind of person — someone who wants to be pushed by great people, build things that outlast a sprint cycle, and go home knowing the work connected back to something real.

The Role

The Senior Talent Acquisition Partner leads end-to-end recruitment across the organization, with a focus on complex, confidential, and leadership roles, and delivers talent acquisition programs and initiatives owned by the Manager, Talent Acquisition. Reporting to the Manager, Talent Acquisition, this role works independently, applying executive presence, sound judgement, critical thinking, and market insight to partner with senior leaders, including the C-suite, on hiring strategy and to solve complex hiring challenges. The Senior Talent Acquisition Partner also serves as a subject matter expert and informal coach to the team and supports the Manager on Executive and VP searches.

What You Do

  • Partner with executives and senior leaders to understand current and future hiring needs and shape role requirements, hiring plans, and selection decisions.

  • Manage the full-cycle recruitment process for roles across the organization, leading Senior Manager, Director, and other business-critical searches, including confidential searches and select mandates assigned by the Manager, TA.

  • Develop and execute proactive sourcing and talent-mapping strategies for senior talent, including passive outreach, networking, and pipelining.

  • Deliver a high-quality, high-touch candidate experience for senior candidates.

  • Use recruitment metrics and market and compensation intelligence to advise leaders and inform hiring strategy.

  • Lead the planning and delivery of talent acquisition initiatives and programs owned by the Manager, TA, managing scope, timelines, stakeholders, and results.

  • Apply critical thinking to challenge assumptions, identify gaps, and recommend improvements to recruitment processes, tools, and systems.

  • Use AI-enabled tools and automation to improve recruiting effectiveness and productivity, with human judgement applied to hiring decisions.

  • Support hiring manager training and enablement, including structured interviewing and inclusive hiring practices.

  • Act as a subject matter expert and informal coach to the Talent Acquisition team on best practices and complex searches.

  • Support the Manager, TA on Executive and VP searches and other select mandates.

  • Ensure compliance with employment laws and internal policies related to hiring and candidate data privacy across relevant jurisdictions.

  • Perform other related duties as assigned to support team objectives, departmental needs, and overall organizational priorities.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in recruitment or talent acquisition, including recruiting Senior Manager and Director roles, ideally in a technology or software environment.

  • Demonstrated executive presence, with the credibility to advise and influence C-suite and senior leaders.

  • Proven success delivering talent acquisition initiatives or programs from planning through implementation, with strong project management and critical thinking skills.

  • Experience using AI-enabled recruiting tools and automation to improve efficiency and outcomes, with sound judgement in how they are applied.

  • Strong understanding of sourcing techniques, applicant tracking systems (preferably Greenhouse), and recruitment analytics, with the business acumen to apply analytics in advising leaders.

  • Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to partner effectively across all levels of the organization.

  • A collaborative, adaptable mindset with a focus on continuous improvement and service excellence.

Note: This position requires a security clearance from the Government of Canada. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada and must successfully obtain and maintain a Reliability security clearance. Please note that specific customer contracts may impose additional security verification requirements. Obtaining and maintaining all required security clearances is a condition of employment. For more information on the Government of Canada's security screening process, please visit Public Services and Procurement Canada.

Versaterm is committed to fair and equitable compensation that is competitive, consistent, and aligned with the value each role contributes to our organization. The starting salary for this position will be dependent upon many factors, such as the successful candidate’s skills, experience, education, training as well as internal equity, market data, and business needs. In addition to base salary and our comprehensive benefits offering, some roles may also be eligible for variable compensation such as incentive plans or discretionary performance bonuses.

AI is central to how Versaterm builds and delivers solutions for our customers. Within Talent Acquisition, we use AI-enabled tools to support certain aspects of the recruitment process, helping our team work more efficiently and spend more time connecting with great talent. AI supports our work, but all hiring and employment decisions are made by people.

Versaterm is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to equity, diversity, inclusion, and a barrier-free workplace. Accommodations are available upon request throughout all stages of the recruitment process and apply to the terms and conditions of employment. For more information, please contact .

jobs.title: Research Engineer, AI
jobs.excerpt: Company Overview Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary

Lead applied research in one or more Orbis AI focus areas — agentic AI, knowledge representation, dynamic ontologies, autonomous analysis, and high-performance analytics — and carry the results into the product. You will frame the problem, survey what already exists, build prototypes that test a real hypothesis, and measure honestly enough to act on the answer. The role exists because our advantage comes from turning advanced research into dependable mission capability.

Travel: Up to 20% for conferences, customer engagement, and team collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

  • Frame research problems drawn from real product and mission gaps, define what a result must show to be worth productizing, and survey existing work before building.
  • Build prototypes that isolate the question being asked, at the fidelity the question actually requires.
  • Run rigorous experiments — baselines, ablations, held-out evaluation, and honest error analysis — with methodology another engineer can reproduce.
  • Build and maintain the datasets and evaluation harnesses your area depends on, including cases that capture known failure modes.
  • Report results clearly, negative results included, and make a defensible recommendation to continue, pivot, or stop.
  • Transition validated results into production alongside product engineers, staying involved through the handoff rather than delivering a notebook.
  • Contribute to the scientific community through publications, open-source releases, and academic collaborations, and advise Orbis on what in the field is worth adopting.
  • Travel up to 20% for conferences, customer engagement, and team collaboration.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of applied research or research-engineering experience, or an M.S./Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field with equivalent applied work
  • Strong Python engineering skills, producing research code another engineer can read, run, and build on
  • Demonstrated experience designing and running experiments that produced an actionable conclusion, with methodology you can defend
  • Depth in at least one Orbis AI focus area: agentic AI, knowledge representation, dynamic ontologies, autonomous analysis, or high-performance analytics
  • Working knowledge of modern LLM and retrieval methods and their practical limitations
  • Clear technical writing that makes a result legible to engineers and non-specialist stakeholders alike
  • Willingness to travel up to 20%

Desired Qualifications

  • Publication record, open-source contributions, or academic collaborations in a relevant area
  • Experience carrying a research result all the way into a production system
  • Experience with knowledge graphs, ontology engineering, reasoning systems, or information extraction
  • Experience with agent architectures, planning, or multi-agent coordination
  • Experience with model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation at scale
  • Experience with performance engineering on data-intensive or analytical workloads
  • Familiarity with OSINT, intelligence, or investigative research workflows

Physical Requirements

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Participation in virtual and in-person meetings
  • Ability to attend planned meetings and/or work in classified spaces for extended periods within the specified work regions
  • Travel: Up to 20% for conferences, customer engagement, and team collaboration.

Orbis Benefits

Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter; the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. From competitive retirement matching to a PTO policy that encourages real time off, we're committed to creating an environment where our team can do their best work and still have a life outside of it.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. A full list of benefits is shared with candidates following an initial conversation with our HR team, so you'll have a clear picture of the support and resources available to you as part of the Orbis team.

Orbis Locations

Orbis works in whatever arrangement the mission requires. Depending on the role, that might mean five days a week on a customer site, full-time in one of our offices, a hybrid schedule, or fully remote work; our team is spread across 25 states and four countries to match. We make sure every team member has the tools and access needed to do the work, wherever that work happens.

Travel is common across many Orbis roles, particularly those supporting customer missions in the field.

Orbis is headquartered in McLean, VA, with additional office locations in Taipei, Taiwan, and Canberra, Australia.

Orbis is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment, and we make employment decisions based on merit,

qualifications, and business need. Orbis does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Orbis complies with all applicable equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws in every jurisdiction in which we operate. Reasonable accommodation is available to applicants and employees with disabilities upon request.

jobs.excerpt: Company Overview Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary

Own product surfaces end to end across the Orbis AI portfolio — the Agent Catalog, the OSINT Agent Harness, and Pulse Analytics — from data model through the interface an analyst actually uses. You will build where AI capability meets a real user: streaming agent output, knowledge structures that change underneath you, and results that must be explainable rather than merely plausible. The role exists because mission users judge our products by what they can see, verify, and act on.

Travel: Up to 15% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and ship features end to end — data model, service logic, API surface, and the user-facing interface that consumes them.
  • Build and own the real-time surfaces of the products: streaming agent output, live task status, and progressive rendering of long-running analysis.
  • Make results explainable in the product by surfacing source, provenance, and reasoning path, so a user can judge a conclusion instead of trusting it.
  • Build interfaces over dynamic ontologies and knowledge structures that stay navigable as the underlying representation evolves.
  • Guarantee the service contracts you expose — versioning, backward compatibility, and failure semantics that consuming teams can rely on.
  • Set quality standards for the surfaces you own, including test coverage, accessibility, and front-end performance budgets.
  • Mentor junior engineers and lead design review and planning for the subsystems you own.
  • Travel up to 15% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional full-stack engineering experience with demonstrated ownership of production product surfaces
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience
  • Strong TypeScript/JavaScript across server and browser runtimes, or a strong Python back end paired with real front-end skill
  • Production experience with a modern front-end framework (React preferred), including component architecture, state management, and rendering performance
  • Working knowledge of API design, including versioning, error contracts, authentication, and authorization
  • Hands-on experience with real-time client-server patterns such as WebSockets, server-sent events, or streaming HTTP
  • Willingness to travel up to 15%

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience presenting complex, interrelated data such as entities, relationships, graphs, timelines, or cited documents
  • Familiarity with LLM application patterns, including streaming responses, retrieval, tool calling, and structured output
  • Experience with graph databases or knowledge representation, and querying them at interactive latency
  • Experience building SDKs or developer-facing libraries where other engineers are the customer
  • Experience packaging and deploying to on-premises, disconnected, or edge environments (Docker, Kubernetes, offline installation)
  • Familiarity with accessibility standards (Section 508 / WCAG) in a government or enterprise context
  • Prior experience in a mission, government, or regulated environment where operational reliability is foundational

Physical Requirements

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Participation in virtual and in-person meetings
  • Ability to attend planned meetings and/or work in classified spaces for extended periods within the specified work regions
  • Travel: Up to 15% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Orbis Benefits

Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter; the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. From competitive retirement matching to a PTO policy that encourages real time off, we're committed to creating an environment where our team can do their best work and still have a life outside of it.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. A full list of benefits is shared with candidates following an initial conversation with our HR team, so you'll have a clear picture of the support and resources available to you as part of the Orbis team.

Orbis Locations

Orbis works in whatever arrangement the mission requires. Depending on the role, that might mean five days a week on a customer site, full-time in one of our offices, a hybrid schedule, or fully remote work; our team is spread across 25 states and four countries to match. We make sure every team member has the tools and access needed to do the work, wherever that work happens.

Travel is common across many Orbis roles, particularly those supporting customer missions in the field.

Orbis is headquartered in McLean, VA, with additional office locations in Taipei, Taiwan, and Canberra, Australia.

jobs.excerpt: At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love.
jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Consultant, Stars Consulting Center of Excellence

Why We Have This Role

At Qualtrics, we help organizations understand people’s experiences and use those insights to drive meaningful clinical, operational, and quality improvements. Following the integration of Press Ganey into Qualtrics, our Stars Consulting Center of Excellence brings together deep healthcare expertise and industry-leading experience management capabilities. As a Medicare Stars Consultant, you’ll be a hands-on practitioner who builds the analyses and deliverables powering consulting engagements across CAHPS, HEDIS, HOS, medication adherence, and operational measures. Working directly with health plans, medical groups, and consulting colleagues, you’ll identify performance gaps, execute complex workstreams independently, and help clients improve the experiences and outcomes of their Medicare Advantage members.

How You’ll Find Success

  • Turn analysis into action: Go beyond reporting results to personally execute deep-dive analytics, explain what’s driving performance, and build practical recommendations clients can implement.
  • Take ownership as a hands-on doer: Clarify the expected outcome, gather the right context, and drive complex workstreams and deliverables forward independently with minimal oversight.
  • Make complex information clear: Translate CMS Stars requirements, technical measure specifications, and analytical findings into compelling stories and recommendations different audiences can understand.
  • Build trusted relationships: Serve as a direct, credible point of contact for client workstreams—listening closely, following through on commitments, and communicating progress, risks, and recommendations early.
  • Stay focused as priorities shift: Balance multiple high-demand client engagements and tight deadlines while maintaining high analytical quality and attention to detail.
  • Help others learn: Create and deliver engaging training that gives health plan teams the knowledge and confidence to apply Stars and member experience best practices.
  • Work collaboratively: Bring together the right internal resources (including Qualtrics/Press Ganey data assets and Hyperlift analytics) and client stakeholders, establish clear responsibilities, and keep delivery moving.

How You’ll Grow

  • Deepen your expertise across Medicare Stars measures and the connections between member experience, clinical quality, and health outcomes.
  • Strengthen your end-to-end consulting skills through autonomous, client-facing data execution, executive presentations, training, and relationship management.
  • Expand your ability to translate CMS guidance, rate announcements, and technical changes into practical client strategies.
  • Develop your ability to integrate member experience insights (CAHPS/HOS) with clinical quality and operational analytics platforms like Hyperlift to inform high-impact improvement decisions.

Things You’ll Do

  • Construct and lead measure-level analytics: Help clients focus on their highest-impact Stars opportunities by executing measure-level performance trending, cut point and gap analyses, and member experience driver analyses across CAHPS, HEDIS, HOS, medication adherence, and operational measures.
  • Design achievable improvement plans: Partner with health plans and medical groups to assess clinical and operational processes, interpret data to identify underlying problems, and recommend targeted interventions.
  • Manage end-to-end workstream delivery: Deliver engagements that meet agreed expectations by managing defined scopes, work plans, timelines, deliverables, budgets, and outcomes while coordinating internal and client resources.
  • Lead client-ready deliverable creation: Build client confidence in decisions and next steps by serving as the direct contact for assigned workstreams and personally preparing data analyses, assessments, quality reviews, and executive presentations.
  • Deliver training and knowledge transfer: Help clients sustain improvements by designing and leading training sessions on Stars, member experience best practices, and process improvement.
  • Monitor regulatory changes and integrate insights: Keep client recommendations current and evidence-based by tracking CMS guidance, rate announcements, and technical specification updates, and integrating Stars analyses with Hyperlift analytics and CAHPS/HOS survey insights.

What We’re Looking For On Your Resume

  • Hands-on experience supporting Medicare Advantage quality, Star Ratings, or member experience work, typically developed through 2+ years in a health plan quality/analytics role or healthcare consulting environment.
  • Demonstrated contributions to performance improvement initiatives with health plan stakeholders, including the specific programs you owned, analytical actions you took, and measurable outcomes you produced.
  • Direct experience in one or more of these areas:
    • HEDIS operations and rate improvement, including measure specifications, supplemental data, and medical record review.
    • CAHPS and member experience improvement across lines of business.
    • Medication adherence and Part D measures.
    • HOS and health outcomes measurement.
    • Government programs and quality requirements associated with Medicare Stars and NCQA.
  • Strong quantitative and data analysis skills using tools such as Excel, Access, SQL, or SAS, with proven ability to translate complex findings into clear recommendations.
  • Experience independently producing clear, client-ready documents and executive presentations, with advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
  • Evidence of managing multiple competing priorities, meeting strict deadlines, and adapting quickly to changing client requirements.
  • A bachelor’s degree.
  • Strongly preferred: Experience with Special Needs Plans—D-SNP, C-SNP, or I-SNP—including their specific quality, compliance, and member experience considerations.

What You Should Know About This Team

  • We are a high-impact, hands-on consulting team focused on helping clients act on their data—not simply delivering static reports.
  • Our work integrates member experience, health plan quality, and Medicare Stars performance within our Stars Consulting Center of Excellence to solve complex problems from multiple angles.
  • We collaborate directly with major health plans and medical groups, grounding recommendations in their operational realities and member needs.
  • You’ll join a fast-paced, growing practice experiencing strong market demand, offering immediate ownership of meaningful client engagements and close collaboration with senior consulting leaders.
  • This role is remote within the United States, with up to 50% travel as needed to support key client engagements.

Our Team’s Favorite Perks and Benefits

  • 100% Performance based promotions -- not politics or tenure
  • Culture - Incredible work environment - you can wear jeans and bring your dog to the office, anytime
  • Quarterly team activities, winter and summer parties, and lots of Qualtrics swag
The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: While this role is exempt from working in office, our hybrid work model remains elegantly simple for the rest of the company: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life. #remote

Precision for Medicine are looking to hire a Clinical Project Manager / Senior Clinical Project Manager with experience in Oncology who have managed full service clinical trials within a CRO setting to join our global team.

In this pivotal role you will have full service oversight for clinical projects across global/regional (ph I-IV) trials, within Oncology. Accountable for clinical project delivery, oversight of all functional departments, and ensuring agreed timelines, scope, cost and quality.

Involved in all study stages, including proposal strategy, development, costing, and bid defence, and seeing studies through the full cycle to completion, managing the client relationship, project team and budget and timelines throughout.

We offer an amazing high-energy, dedicated, collaborative team members who enjoy a challenge, thrive in the details and flourish in dynamic environments. If you are no stranger to taking charge and seek positive teamwork to deliver extraordinary work, we have an opportunity for you.

  • You will independently lead clinical projects in accordance with the study budget and scope of work. You will use your strong interpersonal and organizational skills to set and achieve objectives in the execution of the projects; both contracted objectives and financial objectives. You may be called upon to run international trials as well.
  • Serve as the primary point-of-contact liaison with the client to provide excellent customer service, including participation in proposal activities and client presentations
  • Liaise with Project Team and senior management of both Precision and sponsors, including C level
  • Handle and lead all aspects of a clinical research trial or trials
  • Total project management for all functional areas including data management, safety, clinical, medical monitoring and biostatistics, etc.
  • Prepare project status updates for clients and management; identifying key deliverables and performance metrics of success and escalation.

  • Degree or similar related life science qualification, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Previous experience in a full service/global Project Management role working in the CRO industry is essential.

    • Experience managing studies within Oncology
    • Working understanding of GCP/ICH guidelines and the clinical development process
  • Ability to drive and availability for domestic and international travel including overnight stays
  • Be able to communicate effectively in the English language both written and spoken
  • Strong presentation skills
  • Proven computer skills (MS Office, MS Project, PowerPoint) and software experience (CTMS, eTMF, EDC, IXRS)

Liftoff’s solutions, including Accelerate, Direct, Monetize, Intelligence, and Vungle Exchange, support over 6,600 mobile businesses across 74 countries in sectors such as gaming, social, finance, ecommerce, and entertainment. You’ll be part of a high-impact engineering team responsible for developing web applications, backing services, APIs and tools that help app developers acquire users, optimize engagement, and drive monetization across millions of devices worldwide.

Your contributions will directly impact the performance, reliability, and scalability of our ad delivery, user acquisition, and analytics products. jobs.title: Senior Manager, Investigations(Full time)
jobs.excerpt: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011.
jobs.description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

About this role

GiveDirectly is looking for an experienced investigator who can establish a function, not just run cases. Concerns and allegations reach us from every program and every country we work in. Each one needs to be triaged and assessed objectively, and to end in appropriate findings and recommendations.

You will manage the newly created Central Intake and Investigations Hub. It is a standalone, independent function that works across the whole organisation. The Hub investigates a range of investigations itself, and supports colleagues elsewhere who handle the rest. You will lead the team and take the most complex investigations yourself.

The bigger initial task is to establish the Hub across the organisation. How it works has been designed and agreed. What it does not yet have is standing. People need to know it exists, bring things to it early, and trust what it concludes. This matters now because GiveDirectly is growing fast. Delivery volume and headcount are both rising, and the way staff concerns are handled needs to grow with them.

Reports to: Director of Safeguarding and Investigations

Manages: Future roles including a Program Manager, Investigations and Program Manager, Intake and Reporting to be recruited once the Senior Manager role has been filled.

Level: Senior Manager

Location: Remote, with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours, and meaningful overlap with US Eastern hours. We can only employ people in certain places at the moment, so it's worth checking our current list of eligible countries to see if yours is included. If you're based elsewhere, it's not an automatic no, but do flag it early with your recruiter. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time.

Travel: Occasional. Team meetings and co-locations, plus travel to a country of operation where an investigation requires it. This is not frequent, but it is not predictable either.

What you'll do

  • Establish a Central Intake and Investigations Hub across the organisation: Take an agreed design and make it something people use. Build the relationships with the People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding, HR Managers and Country Directors to ensure concerns are managed effectively. Refine how intake, triage and allocation work in practice as you learn what holds up.
  • Lead the most complex investigations yourself. Establish the facts, produce the findings report and make recommendations.
  • Set the investigation standard and hold other people to it: Define what a good investigation looks like at GiveDirectly. Provide oversight and support where Internal Audit or Safeguarding lead a staff related matter, and quality assure what comes out of it. Decide what training the organisation needs and set its direction.
  • Own the record and what it tells the organisation: Create and hold the system of record for staff matters. Make sure findings and documentation are captured centrally, whoever led the case. Run regular reporting and calibration with the People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding, Country Directors and ExCo. Sign off on relevant internal and external reporting.
  • Make the function work at scale through the responsible use of technology and data: Shape the design of the case management system and its controls, so that staff investigation records sit only where they should. Find the practical places where automation and AI reduce manual work in triage, documentation and reporting. Build the hub so that growth in concern volume does not simply mean a bigger team.
  • Set up and lead the team: Recruit for, manage and develop a Program Manager, Investigations and the Program Manager, Intake and Reporting. Set their priorities, review their work and build their capability.

What success looks like in 12 to 18 months

  • Concerns reach the hub as a matter of course, from every country and function.
  • People come to the hub early and while a matter is still manageable, because they have found it useful rather than because they were told to.
  • Investigations are handled consistently, whoever leads them, and findings reports hold up when they are challenged.
  • The hub is understood across the organisation as an independent central resource.
  • Internal and External reporting tells its audience something they did not already know about patterns, themes and where risk is concentrating.
  • The People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding and country leadership treat the hub as a resource they rely on rather than a process they comply with.
  • Additional hires for the hub are capable, developing, and the function runs day to day without you in the room.

Why this role

  • You build it. This is a new function with a mandate and a set of agreed boundaries. How it actually works is largely what you make it.
  • Genuine independence. The hub is designed to be objective and to handle complex matters.
  • Breadth. You will work across every function and every country GiveDirectly operates in.
  • It matters. Getting this right protects staff and recipients, and protects the trust that lets GiveDirectly move a great deal of money to people who need it.

What we are looking for:

How you work matters as much as your investigation skills.

  • Trusted by the people you also hold to account. You can tell someone that the handling of a matter was wrong, and still have a strong working relationship with them the following week. People Managers, Internal Audit, Safeguarding and country leadership should want to call you early rather than after things have gone wrong.
  • You motivate and influence people who don't report to you. The Hub has no direct line management over Internal Audit, Safeguarding, the People team or country leadership, and it needs all of them to do the work well. You build the relationships and shape best practice.
  • Impartial, and visibly so. People may try to influence you. You will be told the answer before you have found it. You hold to process and evidence without turning it into a fight, and you record what you could not establish as carefully as what you could.
  • You build what isn't there yet. This function is being shaped by you. You are comfortable where the priorities are clear, but the road to them is not. You would rather design a solution rather than wait to be handed one.
  • You work alongside people. Some of the investigative work is done by other teams, and your expertise is what lifts its quality. You get into the detail with colleagues, you are clear about what good looks like and what still needs doing, and you see it through with them.
  • Steady with difficult material. You work with content of abuse and misconduct without losing sight of the people involved, and without carrying it in ways that wear you down.

On experience, we are looking for:

  • Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity.
  • 5-7 years of experience leading workplace (misconduct) investigations, including matters involving senior staff and allegations of sexual misconduct. You have run these end to end, from terms of reference to findings report.
  • Experience in setting investigation standards and quality assuring other people's work, not only conducting investigations yourself.
  • A working understanding of employee relations and of where an investigation ends and an employment decision begins. You have worked alongside other teams without blurring the lines of responsibility.
  • Experience across multiple countries and legal contexts, including where local law shapes how we may investigate and how staff must be treated.
  • Trauma-informed and survivor-centred practice in how you plan interviews, handle disclosures and support the people involved.
  • Has made technology work for investigative teams. You have set up or improved investigative system, built reporting from case data, or introduced tools that changed how a team worked. You have used AI in professional work and can say where it helped, where it did not, and how you handled confidentiality.
  • Language Requirement: Professional fluency in English, plus professional working proficiency in one of French, Swahili or Portuguese. Investigative interviews are often confidential and conducted in these languages.

Why work at GiveDirectly?

At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including:

  • A positive and supportive team with opportunities for advancement
  • A demonstrated commitment to helping all staff develop and grow
  • A competitive salary, including bonus
  • A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country)
  • Unlimited PTO (that we encourage staff to take!)

Read more about our ongoing diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts here and about our decision to move our central support teams to remote first here.

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

United States

  • Base Salary: $114,660
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 10% of base salary
  • Annual Benefits Stipend: $21,393

United Kingdom

  • Base Salary: £77,600
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 10% of base salary
  • Annual Benefits Stipend: £2,760

Kenya

  • Base Salary: $83,820
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 10% of base salary
  • Annual Benefits Stipend: $8,454

This role is fully remote, so if you are not based in the US, UK or Kenya, we will share an estimated salary benchmark for the country you are based in during the hiring process.

Working at GiveDirectly

GiveDirectly is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant.

Commitment to Safeguarding

As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens.

These efforts help us continue to build and maintain trust with the communities we work with, and prevent abuse to our recipients and staff.

**GD is committed to observing all local, national and international laws that protect people and basic human rights of all. GD is committed to a policy of “zero tolerance when it comes to preventing, reporting, or responding to any form of abuse or exploitation.” and expects anyone who works for GD to uphold the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority.**

Reasonable Accommodations

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible work environment. If you require any accommodations during the application or interview process, or to perform the essential functions of the role, please email us at with the email subject “Accommodation Needed”. We will work with you to ensure reasonable accommodations are made to support your needs.

Want to put your best foot forward on your GiveDirectly application? Take a look at our Candidate Application Prep Guide!

Referrals

Know the right person for this role? Please consider referring them. We offer a reward of $3,000 for a Senior Manager or above role, and $500 for a Manager role, paid if we end up hiring your referral. Thank you for sending great people our way!

jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.excerpt: Company Overview Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary

Lead the engineering team behind the Orbis AI portfolio — the Agent Catalog, the OSINT Agent Harness, and Pulse Analytics — and be accountable for what it puts in front of users. You will grow a team of software and research engineers, set the cadence that turns applied research into deployed capability, and hold the line on the accuracy, explainability, and reliability that mission work demands. This role exists because Orbis AI is measured on capability delivered to users, not on experiments run.

Travel: Up to 20% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and grow a team of software and research engineers, owning hiring, onboarding, performance, and career development.
  • Own the team's delivery commitments end to end — scope, sequence, and land work each cycle, surfacing status and risk early rather than at the deadline.
  • Drive the research-to-product path: set direction with product management, define what a result must demonstrate to become a roadmap commitment, and stop work that is not paying off.
  • Enforce the Orbis AI product principles — accuracy and trustworthiness, security and data sovereignty, rapid iteration, deploy anywhere, explainability, and performance — in design review rather than after release.
  • Establish engineering standards that hold under pressure: design and code review, testing, observability, on-call, and incident follow-through.
  • Guide architecture for systems that must run in cloud, on-premises, and edge environments from a single codebase.
  • Clear cross-team blockers — dependencies, interface contracts, and competing priorities — with the product teams that consume Orbis AI capabilities.
  • Travel up to 20% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Required Qualifications

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 2+ years directly managing engineers
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience
  • Track record of delivering meaningful product surfaces on committed timelines
  • Technical depth in distributed systems, backend services, or AI and data platforms sufficient to lead design review credibly
  • Demonstrated ability to grow engineers, including leveling, performance conversations, and hiring against a bar
  • Clear written and verbal communication with both engineering and non-engineering audiences
  • Willingness to travel up to 20%

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience managing teams building agentic AI, LLM-backed products, or knowledge-representation and retrieval systems
  • Experience managing or partnering closely with applied research, and judgment about when a result is ready to productize
  • Experience shipping software into constrained environments such as on-premises, disconnected, or edge deployments
  • Familiarity with containerized deployment (Docker, Kubernetes) across cloud, on-premises, and edge targets
  • Prior experience in a government, national security, or otherwise regulated environment
  • Experience with high-performance analytics or data-intensive systems operating close to the user and the data

Physical Requirements

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Participation in virtual and in-person meetings
  • Ability to attend planned meetings and/or work in classified spaces for extended periods within the specified work regions
  • Travel: Up to 20% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Orbis Benefits

Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter; the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. jobs.title: Regulatory Manager / Senior Regulatory Manager
jobs.excerpt: Precision for Medicine is not your typical CRO.  At Precision for Medicine we have brought together new technologies, expertise and operational scale to help the life sciences improve the speed, cost and success rate of bringing life-changing therapies to patients.
jobs.description:
Precision for Medicine is not your typical CRO. At Precision for Medicine we have brought together new technologies, expertise and operational scale to help the life sciences improve the speed, cost and success rate of bringing life-changing therapies to patients. What sets us apart is the way we integrate clinical trial execution with deep scientific knowledge, laboratory expertise and advanced data sciences. We have a strong focus on Oncology and Rare Disease.

Precision for Medicine are recruiting a Regulatory Manager / Senior Regulatory Manager (depending on experience) to join our growing global team.

As a Regulatory Manager, you will provide regulatory strategy and development guidance for optimal conduct of clinical trials, regulatory agency meetings, orphan designations, paediatric planning, and accelerated procedures, ensuring timely preparation of well organised, quality regulatory submissions in compliance with applicable regulations. You will be responsible for coordinating and preparing regulatory documents for submission to Regulatory Authorities and/or Ethics Committees, as applicable.

Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to:

  • Provides regulatory guidance throughout the clinical development life cycle
  • Compile, coordinate and review applications to Regulatory Authorities including, but not limited to, CTA/IND, annual reports, routine amendments, scientific advice/regulatory authority meetings, orphan designations, paediatric planning, and marketing applications. Also provides strategic regulatory input as required
  • Develops and/or reviews documents intended for submission to the Regulatory Authorities and/or Ethics Committees to assure compliance with regulatory standards
  • Serve as representative of Global Regulatory Affairs at project team meetings with both external and internal customers
  • Works within a project team, and where necessary, leads project for the region or globally
  • Oversee and coordinate Regulatory Affairs Specialists to achieve submission targets for contracted programs
  • Maintenance of project plans, project trackers and regulatory intelligence tools as it pertains to assigned responsibilities and to keep Regulatory Leadership updated.
  • Assist in development of Regulatory Affairs Specialists and other operational area staff, as required
  • Provide input, as required, into regulatory strategy and timeline development for new study opportunities Assists in establishing company standards to ensure the highest quality of submitted information
  • Participates in maintaining and executing on the corporate quality initiatives across business units within clinical solutions.
  • Keeps abreast and continually expand knowledge of laws, regulations and guidelines governing drug development and approval
  • Provides ICH GCP guidance, advice and training to internal and external clients
  • Serve as representative of Global Regulatory Affairs at business development meetings

The ideal candidate will have the following:

Minimum Required:

  • Bachelors degree, or equivalent experience, ideally in a scientific or healthcare discipline
  • 5 years Regulatory experience required for the Manager level and 7 years Regulatory experience required for the Senior Manager Regulatory level
  • Informed knowledge of all aspects of the drug development process inclusive of regulatory milestones and specialised knowledge of regulatory activities for at least one major region (EU, US) including but not limited to submissions to Regulatory Authorities, including INDs/CTAs and amendments, Scientific Advice Procedures, and post-approval submissions.
  • Candidates must have regulatory affairs experience working for a CRO or within the Pharmaceutical Industry, and have experience leading Clinical Submissions
    • Ability to understand clinical and pre-clinical study results, to help in its interpretation for regulatory positions and strategy
    • Knowledgeable of clinical trials methodology, including a working knowledge of protocols and indications being studied
    • Knowledge and expertise with relevant regulations and guidance supporting pharmaceutical development
    • Availability for domestic and international travel including overnight stays

Competencies

  • Strong interpersonal skills and a proven ability to contribute to a team environment involving balancing the demands stemming from multifaceted research activities
  • Understanding of financial management
  • Demonstrates an acceptable degree of professionalism, as evidenced by punctuality, ability to deliver on commitments, an understanding of the service culture and positive interactions with customers and teammates
  • Ability to manage multiple and varied tasks in a fast-moving environment, good record-keeping skills
  • Exhibits high self-motivation, and is able to work and plan independently as well as in a team environment
  • Motivates other members of the project team to meet timelines and project goals
  • Flexible attitude with respect to work assignments, and new learning
  • Resolves project related problems and prioritize workload to meet deadlines with little support from management
  • Focuses on continuous improvement, including the ability to make proactive assessments on how to make processes more efficient and people more effective
  • Collects data of consistently high standard
  • Communicates effectively in the English language both verbally and in written form
  • Conducts formal presentations to a wide variety of audiences including colleagues, investigative staff, and clients with a high level of proficiency

We invite you to learn more about our growing organization serving our clients that are researching ground breaking cancer therapies. We strive to ensure employees feel appreciated for the contributions they make every single day. You will provide input and have your ideas valued and nurtured, impacting positive change for the company.

jobs.excerpt: Precision for Medicine is a global Clinical Research Organization with uniquely integrated offering which enables the science of precision medicine by combining novel clinical trial designs, industry-leading operational and medical experts, advanced biomarker and data analytics solutions, and an unequivocal real passion for rare diseases and oncology, in addition to working across other therapeutic areas.
jobs.description:
Precision for Medicine is a global Clinical Research Organization with uniquely integrated offering which enables the science of precision medicine by combining novel clinical trial designs, industry-leading operational and medical experts, advanced biomarker and data analytics solutions, and an unequivocal real passion for rare diseases and oncology, in addition to working across other therapeutic areas.

Due to our continued growth we are seeking a Regulatory and Start Up Specialist based in the UK to join our growing team. Apart from the experience with regulatory submissions, candidates will ideally also have contracts and budgets negotiation experience for the UK.

Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to:

Responsible for delivery, in terms of timeliness and quality, of site activation readiness within the assigned country/sites and foreseeing and mitigating any risks.

  • Preparation of Clinical Trial Application Forms as well as preparation of submission dossier (initial and amendments/notifications) for submission to Competent Authorities, Ethics Committees, and other applicable local bodies according to local requirements and within required timelines to obtain all necessary authorizations/approvals for the conduct of the Clinical Trial according to international and local/national applicable regulations, company SOPs and principles of ICH-GCP.
  • Interaction with CA/EC for study purposes and handling responses to the CA/EC.
  • Providing regular updates about CA and EC submissions to the Start Up Lead and/or Regulatory Lead assigned to the study and to Project Manager/Project Team
  • Maintenance of project plans, project trackers and regulatory intelligence tools as it pertains to assigned responsibilities and to keep Regulatory Leadership
  • Preparation/Support the development of study specific start-up plans, IMP release requirements and essential document review criteria.
  • Partner with the assigned site CRA to ensure alignment in communication and secure site
  • Review and manage collection of essential documents required for site activation/IMP release.
  • Customize country/site specific Patient Information Sheet and Informed Consent Form.
  • Responsible for/facilitates the translation and co-ordination of translations for documents.
  • Maintain communication with other key functions participating to country start up e., Feasibility, Clinical Operations, Project Management, Regulatory, and Site Contracts management group on project specific status and deliverables.
  • Act as SME for collection and maintenance of site level critical path to Site Activation data points, including but not limited to Competent Authority, local IRB/Ethics Committee (EC) timelines, site contracts and budget negotiation requirements for and other required reviews to secure on time site activation for the assigned sites in the country.
  • When required, participate/support the negotiation of study budgets and the execution of investigator contracts under directions of Site Contract Management department/designee department.
  • May participate/support feasibility group in site outreach to assess potential interest of investigators to a potential study.
  • Keep an updated knowledge of the local clinical trial laws, regulations and help distributing their knowledge within PFM to ensure the conduct of Clinical Trials according to international and local/national applicable regulations.
  • Maintain audit/inspection readiness at all times and file documents as per TMF plan and/ or study specific plans in the relevant TMF
  • May support the clinical team performing Pre-Study Site Visits.

The ideal candidate will have:

Minimum Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or related field (ideally in a scientific or healthcare discipline), or Registered Nurse (RN) or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
  • A qualification in Pharmacy/ work experience as a Pharmacist would be highly beneficial.
  • At least 2 years of relevant experience.

Other Required:

  • Previous experience working as a Regulatory and Start Up Specialist or Site Contracts Specialists in either a CRO or pharmaceutical/ biotech industry or equivalent, relevant experience and/or demonstrated competencies.
  • Strong communication and organizational skills.
  • Experience using computerized information systems, electronic spreadsheets, word processing and electronic mail required.
  • Fluency in English

Preferred:

  • Relevant regulatory and site start-up (feasibility, contract negotiations, CA/ EC/ IRB submissions) experience.
  • Experience in site contract and budget negotiation would be a strong plus.
  • Experience using milestone tracking tools/systems.
  • Ability to prioritize workload to meet deadlines
  • Advanced degree in medical or life sciences (MD, PhD, PharmD)/RAC certification/Masters in Regulatory Science.
